patients.summary: Retired long-haul truck driver with poorly controlled hypertension, COPD and hyperlipidemia who joined in 2022. In late 2025 he had an MI with a stent, then an acute left popliteal occlusion treated with thromboembolectomy and fasciotomy; in June 2026, a week after his last practice visit, an intracerebral hemorrhage led to intubation and ventilator-associated pneumonia, and the practice knows the rest only from faxed notes and a case manager's call.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
65M establishing care. Previous office closing. Brought a grocery bag of bottles and both inhalers.

HPI: Hypertension for years, on lisinopril 10. Doesn't check at home, no cuff. Prior notes show readings in the 150s more often than not. No headaches, no chest discomfort, no swelling. COPD: gets winded on a flight of stairs or carrying groceries in from the truck, has to stop partway up his basement steps. Morning cough, clear sputum. Uses the Spiriva capsule every morning, albuterol maybe 3-4 times a week. No ER trips or steroid bursts for his lungs he can remember in the last couple of years. Never had breathing tests that he recalls. Cholesterol on atorvastatin 40, no muscle aches.

PMH: HTN, COPD, high cholesterol.
PSH: none.
Meds: lisinopril 10 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily, albuterol 2 puffs q4h prn.
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: father had a heart attack at 61. Mother had a brain bleed at 74. One sibling with blood pressure and type 2 diabetes.
SH: drove long-haul for 30-some years, retired. Smoked from his late teens, a pack and more a day on the road, about 40 pack-years, quit in 2016 and stayed quit. Doesn't drink at all. Divorced, lives alone in Westfield, drives.

Exam: BP high today, repeat similar (see vitals). Comfortable at rest, speaks full sentences. No JVD. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs: diminished breath sounds throughout, mild prolonged expiration, no wheeze, no crackles. Abdomen benign, no pulsatile mass. Legs: no edema, pedal pulses 2+ both feet. Neuro grossly intact.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
1. HTN, above goal on lisinopril 10. Office reading only, no home numbers. Recheck next visit; asked him to pick up a home cuff. CMP today.
2. COPD, group B by prior notes. No spirometry on file: ordering full spirometry with bronchodilator. Continue tiotropium, albuterol prn. Inhaler technique reviewed with the capsule device, he does it well.
3. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40. Lipids today.
4. Former heavy smoker: qualifies for yearly low-dose CT. Ordered. Also one-time aortic ultrasound for AAA screening.
5. Health maintenance: colonoscopy 2019 normal, due 2029. PCV20 and Tdap given today. Hep C and HIV screening today, A1c with sibling's diabetes. Flu and COVID when the fall vaccines arrive.
RTC 4-5 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Gordon, your labs from Tuesday look fine. Kidney function and potassium are normal on the lisinopril, blood counts normal, sugar and A1c normal, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. Cholesterol numbers are about where I'd expect on atorvastatin 40, no change. The breathing test and the scans are being scheduled, our staff will call you.

reports.text: Pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry, albuterol 4 puffs via spacer. Acceptable and repeatable effort. Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.64. Post-bronchodilator FEV1 68% of predicted. No significant bronchodilator response. CAT score 14. mMRC dyspnea grade 2.
reports.conclusion: Fixed airflow obstruction consistent with COPD. Symptom burden and exacerbation history fit GOLD group B.

documents.title: Spirometry interpretation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spirometry reviewed. Ratio 0.64 after albuterol with FEV1 68% predicted, no reversibility. CAT 14, mMRC 2, no exacerbations in the past year. COPD, group B. Long-acting antimuscarinic alone is reasonable; stay on tiotropium daily with albuterol as needed. Will revisit if his breathing worsens or he needs rescue more than a few times a week.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
68M, seen after a hospital stay for MI.

What we have: his account and the medication sheet he brought. No discharge summary yet despite our request on 11/21; re-requested today.
Per patient: on 11/17 he felt unwell in the chest, called 911, told it was a heart attack, went for a catheterization the same day and got one stent. Doesn't know which artery. Home 11/20. Since then no chest pain, no palpitations, no fainting. Tired, walking in the house and to the mailbox. Breathing at his baseline.

Meds reconciled against the hospital sheet and the fill history:
- aspirin EC 81 mg daily (new, hospital)
- metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily (new, hospital)
- lisinopril 10 mg daily
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily
- tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
- albuterol HFA 2 puffs q4h prn
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted, pulse slower than his usual on the beta-blocker, BP still above goal. Comfortable. Neck without JVD. Heart regular, no murmur or rub. Lungs diminished, no crackles. Groin and wrist without hematoma (he isn't sure where they went in). Legs no edema, feet warm, pedal pulses present.

A/P
1. CAD with recent MI, s/p PCI with drug-eluting stent 11/17/25. Problem list updated. Continue the hospital regimen as above. Cardiology follow-up was arranged by the hospital; he'll get a call. Chest pain warning signs reviewed, 911.
2. HTN, still above goal now on metoprolol plus lisinopril 10. Will look again after cardiology weighs in.
3. COPD B, stable.
4. Hyperlipidemia, atorvastatin 40.
RTC after the cardiology visit, sooner if needed.

conditions.label: Acute embolism and thrombosis of left lower extremity artery
conditions.note: left popliteal occlusion; thromboembolectomy with fasciotomy

documents.title: Emergency Department Note (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Seen 12/08/2025, received by fax 12/10/2025.

CC: left leg pain, sudden.
HPI: 68-year-old man three weeks out from MI with a drug-eluting stent, woke with abrupt, severe left lower-leg pain, sharp and constant. Noticed the foot looked white and felt cold. No fall or injury.
PMH: HTN, COPD, CAD s/p recent MI and PCI, hyperlipidemia.
Meds: aspirin, atorvastatin, metoprolol succinate, lisinopril, tiotropium, albuterol prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit about 10 years ago. No alcohol. Retired trucker.

VS stable, afebrile.
Exam: left foot pulse diminished relative to the right. Left foot cool, cap refill delayed, sensation decreased. Dorsiflexion and plantar flexion 3/5 on the left.
Labs: CBC within normal limits. Creatinine 1.1. Troponin not elevated. D-dimer elevated.
Doppler US, left lower extremity: abrupt cutoff of arterial flow at the left popliteal artery.
ABI left 0.5.

Impression: acute arterial occlusion, left popliteal, thrombotic or embolic, threatened limb.
Disposition: vascular surgery at bedside; to the OR for left femoral-popliteal thromboembolectomy with fasciotomy. Admitted to vascular surgery.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back after a second hospital stay in a month.

We have the ED note only (faxed 12/10); no operative note or discharge summary. Re-requested.
Per patient: the morning of 12/8 his left lower leg went suddenly painful and the foot white and cold. Taken to the OR that day by vascular surgery, who cleared the clot from the artery and opened the calf to relieve the pressure (fasciotomy). Home 12/13. A visiting nurse comes for dressing changes. Vascular surgery follow-up is set by the hospital for early January.
No chest pain. Breathing at baseline.
Meds per patient and bottles: unchanged from 12/1 (aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 10, atorvastatin 40, tiotropium, albuterol). Nothing new from this admission he knows of.

Exam: BP above goal. Comfortable. Heart regular. Lungs diminished, no crackles. Left leg: dressings over the calf clean and dry, left in place for the visiting nurse; groin incision clean, no drainage. Left foot warm and pink, cap refill brisk. Right foot normal. Walks unaided across the room.

A/P
1. Acute arterial embolism/thrombosis, left popliteal, s/p femoral-popliteal thromboembolectomy with fasciotomy 12/8. Added to the problem list. Wound care with VNA, vascular follow-up as arranged.
2. CAD, MI 11/17 with stent. Cardiology visit pending.
3. HTN, still above goal; no change for now while he recovers.
4. COPD B stable.
5. The lung screening CT ordered in October is cancelled for now, he has had enough scanning this month; will reorder next fall.
BMP and CBC today. RTC 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 06/19/2026, faxed 06/22/2026. Filed for PCP review.

CC: unresponsive.
HPI: 69-year-old man, history of poorly controlled hypertension, COPD, CAD with MI and stent in 11/2025, hyperlipidemia, and an acute left popliteal arterial occlusion treated surgically in 12/2025. Found unresponsive at home, brought in by EMS. No known trauma.
Meds per pharmacy record: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 10, tiotropium, albuterol prn.
Allergies: NKDA.

Arrival BP 220/120. GCS 6. Pupils reactive and symmetric.
CT head non-contrast: basal ganglia hemorrhage extending into the internal capsule with surrounding edema, no midline shift; no crescent- or lens-shaped collection.

Assessment: intracerebral hemorrhage with airway compromise.
Course: intubated in the ED for airway protection, placed on mechanical ventilation. Admitted to the ICU.

documents.title: ICU Progress Note (received)
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital medical ICU. Date of service 06/24/2026, received by fax 06/29/2026. Filed; PCP aware.

69M with HTN, CAD s/p MI/DES, COPD, admitted 6/19 with basal ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage and airway compromise, intubated on arrival, now ventilator day 5.
Interval: new fever to 38.9 C in the last 24 hours, increasing purulent secretions from the endotracheal tube, worsening oxygenation.
On norepinephrine; hemodynamically stable on current dose.
Exam: sedated. Diffuse crackles both lungs. Remainder of exam unremarkable.
Labs: WBC 12,000 yesterday, 18,000 today.
CXR: new bilateral infiltrates.
Home meds on file: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 10, tiotropium, albuterol.
Allergies: NKDA.

Assessment: ventilator-associated pneumonia with respiratory failure and septic shock, in the setting of intracerebral hemorrhage.
Plan: blood and respiratory cultures sent; empiric IV antibiotics started; continue vasopressor support and ventilator management.

documents.title: Call from hospital case manager
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Case manager from the regional hospital called to update the PCP office. Mr. Ryan is off the ventilator, off norepinephrine, and finishing his IV antibiotic course. Plan is transfer to an inpatient rehabilitation facility in the coming week. She will send the discharge summary when he leaves. Asked her to include the medication list and to have rehab contact us about a follow-up visit. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP note on call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. Will see him once he is out of rehab. Awaiting discharge summary.

documents.title: Lisinopril auto-refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy auto-refill request for lisinopril 10 mg #90. Patient is inpatient at rehab per hospital case manager. Held per PCP until the post-discharge visit; pharmacy notified.

documents.title: Follow-up visit scheduled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Rehab facility social worker called asking for a primary care follow-up after his expected discharge. Booked Thu 9/17 at 10:00, 40 minutes, hospital follow-up. Asked them to send the hospital discharge summary and the rehab medication list before the visit. Neither received as of today.

documents.title: Discharge summary request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called the hospital records office again for the June admission discharge summary ahead of the 9/17 visit. They show him transferred to rehab in July; summary not yet finalized for release. Request remains open.
